title: Vetala Extended Tale 44: The Prince and the Beggar Boy
summary: "Prince Yashovardhana and a beggar boy named Kalu were trapped on a crumbling mountain ledge when a cloudburst triggered a devastating landslide. The ledge could support the weight...
keywords: vetala extended tale 44: a riddle tale of dharma where vetala tests vikram's sense of justice with story of love, betrayal, and clever decision.
full_text:
Once again, Vikram slung the corpse across his broad shoulder. The Vetala whispered:

"Prince Yashovardhana and a beggar boy named Kalu were trapped on a crumbling mountain ledge when a cloudburst triggered a devastating landslide. The ledge could support the weight of only one person; the rock was shearing away beneath their feet.

The prince possessed royal armor and a fine dagger, while Kalu had only rags. The prince commanded: 'Leap off, pauper! My life is needed to govern a kingdom, whereas your death will not be noticed by a single soul.'

Kalu looked down into the roaring gorge, then looked into the prince's frightened eyes. Without malice, the beggar boy said: 'If your kingdom needs you, go home in safety, Prince.' And with a calm smile, Kalu jumped into the swirling waters below, giving the prince time to scramble to solid ground.

Tell me, Vikramaditya: who was the true prince on that mountain ledge?"

Vikramaditya replied with deep emotion: "The beggar boy Kalu was the true prince. Royalty of birth is an accident of fate, but royalty of character is demonstrated through voluntary sacrifice. The prince showed the pettiness of a coward clinging to life through arrogance, while the pauper boy showed the magnificent sovereignty of a soul capable of dying so another might live."

"Magnificent answer!" laughed the Vetala, slipping away into the black night.
moral: Noble character is born of heroic deeds in times of peril, not of lineage or royal garments.
